english.title: Handle / control / transfer controlled waste without taking reasonable measures - Environmental Protection Act 1990.
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person subject to a duty of care in respect of controlled waste under section 34(1) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 as **(..SPECIFY BASIS OF DUTY..), failed to comply with that duty in that you failed to take all such measures applicable to you in that capacity as were reasonable in the circumstances to

(A)_[prevent a contravention of section 33 of the Act by the unauthorised or harmful deposition, treatment or disposal of waste]_
(B)_[prevent a contravention by another person of regulation 12 of the Environmental Permitting Regulations]_
(C)_[prevent a contravention by another person of a condition of an environmental permit]_
(D)_[prevent the escape of the waste from your control or that of another person]_
(E)_[secure that the transport of waste was only to an authorised person or to a person for authorised transport purposes]_
(F)_[secure that, on the transfer of waste, there was also transferred such a written description of the waste as would enable other persons to avoid a contravention of section 33 of the Act or regulation 12 of the Environmental Permitting Regulations or a contravention of a condition of an environmental permit, and to comply with the duty under section 34(1) of the Act as respects the escape of waste]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 34(1) and (6) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.
Time limit on prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
